sheet.name: Grukka Ironhide
sheet.opening: Grukka Ironhide, a big, scarred Half-Orc barbarian raised in a border-town temple after her orc father's warband left her behind, stands at the edge of the temple's market square at dusk, greataxe on her back, handaxes at her belt, a prayer wheel tucked in her pouch. The old priestess who took her in and taught her prayers (while the other children taught her to fight) is the reason she still calls this place home. Tonight a gang of armed toughs, bold enough to wear a stranger's colors, has cornered a frightened temple acolyte and a pair of market vendors, shaking them down for 'tithes' and smashing the stalls near the temple steps. The priestess's door is barred behind them, and the town watch is nowhere to be seen. Grukka is loud, blunt, and cannot walk past a bully picking on someone smaller, and she has never backed down from a challenge, so the moment demands that she step in, whether she thinks it through first or not.

RULE Dropping to 0 Hit Points:
When you drop to 0 hit points, you either die outright or fall unconscious, as explained in the following sections.

#### Instant Death

Massive damage can kill you instantly. When damage reduces you to 0 hit points and there is damage remaining, you die if the remaining damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum.

For example, a cleric with a maximum of 12 hit points currently has 6 hit points. If she takes 18 damage from an attack, she is reduced to 0 hit points, but 12 damage remains. Because the remaining damage equals her hit point maximum, the cleric dies.

#### Falling Unconscious

If damage reduces you to 0 hit points and fails to kill you, you fall unconscious (see appendix PH-A). This unconsciousness ends if you regain any hit points.

#### Death Saving Throws

Whenever you start your turn with 0 hit points, you must make a special saving throw, called a death saving throw, to determine whether you creep closer to death or hang onto life. Unlike other saving throws, this one isn't tied to any ability score. You are in the hands of fate now, aided only by spells and features that improve your chances of succeeding on a saving throw.

Roll a d20. If the roll is 10 or higher, you succeed. Otherwise, you fail. A success or failure has no effect by itself. On your third success, you become stable (see below). On your third failure, you die. The successes and failures don't need to be consecutive; keep track of both until you collect three of a kind. The number of both is reset to zero when you regain any hit points or become stable.

***Rolling 1 or 20.*** When you make a death saving throw and roll a 1 on the d20, it counts as two failures. If you roll a 20 on the d20, you regain 1 hit point.

***Damage at 0 Hit Points.*** If you take any damage while you have 0 hit points, you suffer a death saving throw failure. If the damage is from a critical hit, you suffer two failures instead. If the damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum, you suffer instant death.

#### Stabilizing a Creature

The best way to save a creature with 0 hit points is to heal it. If healing is unavailable, the creature can at least be stabilized so that it isn't killed by a failed death saving throw.

You can use your action to administer first aid to an unconscious creature and attempt to stabilize it, which requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

A **stable** creature doesn't make death saving throws, even though it has 0 hit points, but it does remain unconscious. The creature stops being stable, and must start making death saving throws again, if it takes any damage. A stable creature that isn't healed regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours.

#### Monsters and Death

Most GMs have a monster die the instant it drops to 0 hit points, rather than having it fall unconscious and make death saving throws.

Mighty villains and special nonplayer characters are common exceptions; the GM might have them fall unconscious and follow the same rules as player characters.

The square stops being a square and turns into a town. The old vendor woman's pail is the first thing to break a bandit's skull. After that come stools, rolling-pins, a fishmonger's boathook, and a hundred shuttered neighbours who've been waiting for someone to go first. The bandits at the tailgate are swallowed by shouting people and go down under them. The three crossbowmen on the temple steps find their targets sliding out of reach and their quarry's door standing open at their backs, and Brother Aldric comes out of it with a bench.

Gaunt, you learn later, does not try to hold the square. He looks at the shutters opening one after another, takes in the numbers, and nods once as though a sum has come out the way he expected. "Another day, Mother," he says, politely, loud enough to carry. "I'm patient. The key will keep." He mounts the black mare, signals Harl, and the column withdraws toward the east gate with the wagons rattling and Pell clutching his ledger to his chest. Nobody is quite brave enough to stop them. You hear all of this later, in pieces, from the boy.

Now you wake with the priestess's palm on your brow and warmth in your chest, a Cure Wounds for 8, and you're at **8 of 15 HP**. It's about 12:35 PM. You're back on the cobbles of the temple square with your greataxe, two handaxes, four javelins and Brother Aldric's tithe satchel beside you, all recovered from the abandoned wagon when the gang fled. Brother Aldric is kneeling at your side, weeping. The old woman is bundling a bleeding bandit with a bedsheet, and the vendor boy is sitting on a barrel with a boathook across his knees and a grin on his face.

Your Rage and Relentless Endurance are spent until a long rest. You've earned **175 XP** (175 of 300). Merra, as far as anyone knows, is still hiding in the river hollow below the toll-house bridge. The old priestess has not let go of your hand.

"Gaunt will be back," she says quietly. "And there's more I should have told you, child, about what sleeps beneath this temple. But first: where is the girl?"

What does Grukka do?

I squeeze her hand and sit up, then tell her everything: the toll-house, the cellar, the culvert, and the hollow under the willow roots where I left Merra. "I'm going to fetch her myself the moment I can stand, Mother, and then you're telling me everything about what's under this temple, starting with why Gaunt wants it." I strap the greataxe on, take a long drink from the boy's waterskin, and check Brother Aldric's satchel is still full of silver.

You tell her everything in a low, rough voice while the square mops itself up around you: the cellar, the culvert, the willow hollow, the black-handprint men and the quiet grey one who cut you down with a thrown dagger and then bound your wound. The old priestess listens with her eyes closed, nodding at the end of each piece like a woman counting beads.

"Merra's alive, then," she says. "That's the best news I've had since dawn. And she'll hold. That girl has more spine than the whole watch." She lifts a hand, and two broad young men from the bakery, the baker's sons, shoulder through the crowd. "Tomas, Wil: take the cart and the mule, go east along the river, under the willow below the toll-house bridge. Bring her home. And keep off the road if you see a grey coat." They nod and are gone. "You'll not outrun a cart on those legs, Grukka, and you'll not be of use to her half dead. Let them go."

The satchel is mostly full. Silver and some copper still jingle in it, though a few coins are plainly missing, which Pell must have pocketed for Gaunt. Brother Aldric blesses you three times and cannot stop thanking you.

Then the priestess draws you into the temple's cool dark, away from the people, and bars the door. In the lamplit nave she lowers her voice. "Under this floor is a crypt older than the town. It holds what our founders chose not to destroy: something bound, sealed by a two-part key. I have one half. The other, child, you've carried since you were small and never known it." Her eyes go to the pouch at your belt where your prayer wheel rests. "I gave it to you to keep it safe from men like Gaunt. I didn't think they'd come this soon."

You're at 8 of 15 HP, without Rage, and still hungry and tired. It's about 1 PM. What does Grukka do?

I pull the prayer wheel out of my pouch and turn it over in my scarred hands, staring at it as if I'd never really seen it. "This? I've spun it a thousand times, Mother. Show me how it's the key, and tell me what's sealed down there and why the founders didn't just destroy it."

The wagons are gone. They halt.

Gaunt's voice floats clear across the dusk, level as a table. "Thornwick! Sergeant Tamm. Good evening. I've no quarrel with you or your neighbours. I want the Ironhide, and I want the tongue and the disc. Hand those over and I'll ride away. Refuse, and I'll still have them, but the cost will be paid in a coin I'd rather not spend." A pause. RULE Melee Attacks:
Used in hand-to-hand combat, a melee attack allows you to attack a foe within your reach. A melee attack typically uses a handheld weapon such as a sword, a warhammer, or an axe. A typical monster makes a melee attack when it strikes with its claws, horns, teeth, tentacles, or other body part. A few spells also involve making a melee attack.

Most creatures have a 5-foot **reach** and can thus attack targets within 5 feet of them when making a melee attack. Certain creatures (typically those larger than Medium) have melee attacks with a greater reach than 5 feet, as noted in their descriptions.

Instead of using a weapon to make a melee weapon attack, you can use an **unarmed strike**: a punch, kick, head-butt, or similar forceful blow (none of which count as weapons). On a hit, an unarmed strike deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1 + your Strength modifier. You are proficient with your unarmed strikes.

#### Opportunity Attacks

In a fight, everyone is constantly watching for a chance to strike an enemy who is fleeing or passing by. Such a strike is called an opportunity attack.

You can make an opportunity attack when a hostile creature that you can see moves out of your reach. To make the opportunity attack, you use your reaction to make one melee attack against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

You can avoid provoking an opportunity attack by taking the Disengage action. You also don't provoke an opportunity attack when you teleport or when someone or something moves you without using your movement, action, or reaction. For example, you don't provoke an opportunity attack if an explosion hurls you out of a foe's reach or if gravity causes you to fall past an enemy.

#### Two-Weapon Fighting

When you take the Attack action and attack with a light melee weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a different light melee weapon that you're holding in the other hand. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

If either weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon, instead of making a melee attack with it.

#### Contests in Combat

Battle often involves pitting your prowess against that of your foe. Such a challenge is represented by a contest. This section includes the most common contests that require an action in combat: grappling and shoving a creature. The GM can use these contests as models for improvising others.

#### Grappling

When you want to grab a creature or wrestle with it, you can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, a grapple. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them.

The target of your grapple must be no more than one size larger than you and must be within your reach. Using at least one free hand, you try to seize the target by making a grapple check instead of an attack roll: a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use). If you succeed, you subject the target to the grappled condition (see appendix PH-A). The condition specifies the things that end it, and you can release the target whenever you like (no action required).

(Athletics) check.

***Moving a Grappled Creature.*** When you move, you can drag or carry the grappled creature with you, but your speed is halved, unless the creature is two or more sizes smaller than you.

#### Shoving a Creature

Using the Attack action, you can make a special melee attack to shove a creature, either to knock it prone or push it away from you. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them.

The target must be no more than one size larger than you and must be within your reach. Instead of making an attack roll, you make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use). If you win the contest, you either knock the target prone or push it 5 feet away from you.

Dropped Grukka with a thrown dagger at the road bend (Day 2, ~8:23 AM). Has ordered his men not to kill her.

Stabilized Grukka himself after she fell (Medicine 10) and took her alive. By ~12:20 PM Day 2 the gang column with Grukka bound in a wagon has reached the temple square in Thornwick; Gaunt demands something of the old priestess at the temple door. Merra was not found at the hollow (as far as Grukka knows).

12:35 PM Day 2: when Thornwick's townsfolk rose against his men, Gaunt withdrew calmly with his column (Harl, Pell, wagons), leaving the square. He said he would return for the key to the old crypt. The chest with Grukka's weapons and Brother Aldric's tithe satchel were left behind in the confusion (recovered).

Merra overheard Gaunt say: the seal 'answers only to a hand that means it' (the disc must be turned willingly by its bearer, or by a hand broken to his will); he intends to bind the Marchwarden with a black glove-relic. This is why he kept Grukka alive and stabilized her. Harl's gang is merely 'a blade to test the temple' and his real strength is yet to come.

A sealed crypt beneath the Thornwick temple, which Gaunt seeks. Locked by a two-part key: the old priestess keeps one part, the other is hinted to be Grukka's prayer wheel. Priestess says it holds something sealed in by the temple's founders.

Priestess's account: the temple's founders sealed a bound war-spirit called the Marchwarden, an ancient defender of the border whose fury turned on its own and could not be destroyed, only put to sleep. The seal needs two parts: the iron tongue (priestess's) and a bronze disc hidden in the inner drum of Grukka's prayer wheel. Gaunt wants to wake it and bind it as a weapon.
An ancient bound war-spirit of the borderlands sealed beneath the Thornwick temple by its founders, who could not destroy it. Its fury turned on those it defended.

Sergeant Corvin Tamm, Thornwick's town watch sergeant, marched his men out of barracks after the captain took Gaunt's coin. Commands nine watchmen, six of them real fighters, loyal to him not the captain.

Hold Thornwick's temple and keep the two halves of the crypt key (iron tongue and bronze disc in Grukka's prayer wheel) from Gaunt, who plans to wake the Marchwarden. Barricade on the east road, Sergeant Tamm's six fighters, bows on the baker's roof, Grukka at the temple door. Gaunt expected tonight.
SECRET: Grukka rolled a natural 1 checking the barricade; she believes it sound but there is an unblocked gap at the tannery alley on the north side of the east road, which Gaunt's scouts will find.

7:55 PM Day 2: Gaunt's column (Harl, eight or nine bandits, Pell, Gaunt) halted a hundred paces from the east-road barricade carrying torches; Grukka on the temple's top step with greataxe and a handaxe, bronze disc in her pouch. Gaunt is calling for parley while a small party scouts the tannery alley.
8:00 PM: Grukka spotted the tannery-alley infiltrators; Tamm posted two spearmen there. Gaunt's parley refused; Harl's men start the charge on the east-road barricade.

8:01 PM Day 2: Grukka dropped to 0 HP at the temple door after killing Harl's cob with a natural 20. Harl is on foot at the steps; two bandits shoot from the square. Tamm's barricade holds somewhere behind.

8:02 PM Day 2: Grukka at 0 HP again with 2 death-save failures on the top step. Brother Aldric was shot by both bandits and struck down by Harl's mace (dead or dying). The old priestess is at Grukka's shoulder in the doorway.

story.text:
STORY SO FAR (start of game to end of turn 42)

PREMISE
Thornwick is a border town on the edge of the wild marches, with a small stone temple in the middle of its market square. Grukka Ironhide is a scarred Half-Orc barbarian (chaotic good), raised in that temple by the Old Priestess after her orc father's warband left her behind. Her ideal is protecting the weak. She charges in before thinking and can't back down from a challenge. The game clock started Day 1, 6:30 PM.

THE MARKET SQUARE (Day 1 dusk)
- Six men of the Ash-Mark Gang (grey sashes with a black handprint, called "the Black Hand") were shaking down an acolyte and two vendors, and smashing stalls.
- Grukka strode in shouting. Harl, the scarred leader (a thug: 32 HP, AC 11, two mace attacks, Pack Tactics), closed and rolled two natural 20s, taking her to 1 HP. Relentless Endurance saved her. Two bandits finished her.
- Harl told his men to leave her ("a dead one brings the watch").
- The vendor boy failed to stabilize her. The Old Priestess succeeded (Medicine 21) and cast Cure Wounds for 11.
- The gang took the acolyte Merra and Brother Aldric's tithe satchel east.
- Priestess info: the gang squats at the abandoned toll-house a mile out on the east road (beside a washed-out bridge), fourteen or more strong. A gang man called Harl "Gaunt's dog".

THE TOLL-HOUSE
- Grukka ate and went out the east gate. She bluffed a sentry as "Dagga, sent by Gaunt's dog" (Deception 14), then slipped on a second answer. A fight followed. She killed the sentry. Four yard bandits shot her to 1 HP.
- She hid behind a wagon and slipped through the toll-house side door into the storeroom. She took a one-hour short rest there unfound and healed to full.
- She crept upstairs and saw: Harl, a bandit guard, Pell (a thin ink-stained clerk with a ledger), Merra bound on a stool, and the tithe satchel on a table.
- She charged in (surprise, advantage). Harl was hit for 10 (22/32). He and a guard beat her to 0 HP. Harl ordered "Don't finish her. Gaunt will want to see this one." She was tied up and her weapons were taken (greataxe, handaxes, javelins into an iron-banded chest).
- Merra stabilized her (Medicine 12). She woke at 1 HP at about 10 PM in the cellar. She sawed her cord on an iron ring in the wall (Athletics 21).
- A guard named Dunn came down. She grappled him and knocked him out with a scimitar pommel, taking his scimitar, light crossbow, bolts and 6 gp. Harl realized the voice was wrong and rebarred the trapdoor.
- She found and tore out a rusted drain grate (Athletics 25) and escaped with Merra through the culvert under the bridge.
- They slept in an undercut riverbank hollow under a willow. A lookout glimpsed movement and a patrol passed. Near midnight she heard a horse with a bell-harness arrive (Gaunt).
- Long rest done: 7:01 AM Day 2, full HP, Rage 2/2 and Relentless Endurance restored.

DAY 2 MORNING
- Merra's info (heard while tied): Gaunt's real interest is "whatever lies beneath the temple". The tithes were a pretext (Pell said so). Gaunt said "the seal answers only to a hand that means it". He wanted "any who'd defend that temple". Merra never saw Gaunt's face.
- Grukka scouted from the alders (Perception nat 1, then a careful 12). She saw the tall black mare with a bell-harness, and a tall lean man in a grey greatcoat with gloves and a silver collar clasp, who watches the Thornwick road. The gang was loading two wagons and leaving for Thornwick.
- She ambushed the column at a road bend (Stealth 8 failed). Gaunt (statted as a bandit captain: 65 HP, AC 15, three attacks with scimitar and dagger, or two thrown daggers, Parry) joined with Harl, an outrider, three foot bandits and two wagon drivers.
- She shot the outrider (3 HP left), raged, and was reduced to 1 HP. Relentless Endurance was spent again. She Disengaged toward the birch and the bank. A foot bandit followed and missed. Gaunt's thrown dagger then dropped her to 0 HP (turn 42's end).
- Gaunt, calm and unhurried, said, "Enough. Nobody touches her. Dunn's wrists and Harl's ribs are the price of that, and I'll collect it from her, not from a corpse." His second Medicine check stabilized her (10). The column took her.

NPCs AND THREADS
- Old Priestess: raised Grukka, uses Cure Wounds (spellcasting mod +3).
- Brother Aldric: an old temple brother. His tithe satchel was stolen. He is devout and weeps easily.
- Merra: young acolyte, brave, still hidden at the willow hollow as of the end of turn 42. Not found by the gang.
- Pell: smooth-voiced clerk (commoner), works for Gaunt, tallies the tithes.
- Dunn: cellar guard, left unconscious and tied in the cellar.
- Gaunt: patient, polite, never raises his voice, wants both key halves, plans to wake and bind the bound war-spirit.
- Harl: bandaged ribs, 22/32 HP at that point. Hates Grukka.
- Open quest: Rescue Merra (Day 2 afternoon she reached town safely, so done).
- Hidden decisions: the gang carries a black-glove relic Gaunt means to use to bind the Marchwarden. Merra will later say what she overheard.

Grukka's sheet at the end of turn 42: 0 HP, unconscious, stable. Rage 1/2 left (one spent on Day 2 morning). Relentless Endurance spent. Hit die available. Gear: greataxe, 2 handaxes, 4 javelins, scimitar, light crossbow and 9 bolts, 21 gp. Bond: the old priestess and the temple.
